item.title: Introduction
item.description: Kafka Streams The easiest way to write mission-critical real-time applications and microservices Kafka Streams is a client library for building applications and microservices, where the input and output data are stored in Kafka clusters. It combines the simplicity of writing and deploying standard Java and Scala applications on the client side with the benefits of Kafka’s server-side cluster technology. item.description: Run Kafka Streams Demo Application This tutorial assumes you are starting fresh and have no existing Kafka or ZooKeeper data. However, if you have already started Kafka, feel free to skip the first two steps. Kafka Streams is a client library for building mission-critical real-time applications and microservices, where the input and/or output data is stored in Kafka clusters. Kafka Streams combines the simplicity of writing and deploying standard Java and Scala applications on the client side with the benefits of Kafka’s server-side cluster technology to make these applications highly scalable, elastic, fault-tolerant, distributed, and much more.

item.title: Core Concepts
item.description: Kafka Streams is a client library for processing and analyzing data stored in Kafka. It builds upon important stream processing concepts such as properly distinguishing between event time and processing time, windowing support, and simple yet efficient management and real-time querying of application state. Kafka Streams has a low barrier to entry : You can quickly write and run a small-scale proof-of-concept on a single machine; and you only need to run additional instances of your application on multiple machines to scale up to high-volume production workloads.

item.title: Upgrade Guide
item.description: Upgrade Guide and API Changes Upgrading from any older version to 3.8.1 is possible: if upgrading from 3.4 or below, you will need to do two rolling bounces, where during the first rolling bounce phase you set the config upgrade.from="older version" (possible values are "0.10.0" - "3.4") and during the second you remove it. This is required to safely handle 3 changes. The first is introduction of the new cooperative rebalancing protocol of the embedded consumer.
